html:
Agostinho Neto was the leader of the MPLA and the first president of Angola, from independence on 11 November 1975 until his death in 1979.

The son of a Methodist pastor, he studied medicine in Portugal, wrote poetry on the suffering of Angolans, and was jailed several times by the Portuguese. He led the MPLA from 1962 in the war of independence.

With help from the Soviet Union and Cuban troops he held Luanda against rival movements and declared independence. In May 1977 a faction under Nito Alves tried to seize power, and the purge that followed killed thousands. He died in Moscow in 1979, and José Eduardo dos Santos succeeded him in a country at war. His birthday is a national holiday in Angola.
